page: OVHcloud b3-640 is a general-purpose server instance powered by an AMD EPYC processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 160 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, operating at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 640 GB of system memory, providing a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is supported by a local 400 GB NVMe SSD, and network connectivity is established with a baseline bandwidth of 20 Gbps.

Benchmark results show top-tier performance in multi-core and highly parallelized operations. The instance achieves top 10% placement in stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, Passmark CPU score, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Memory performance is also strong, with cached small-block read bandwidth reaching 9067.58 GB/sec and uncached large-block read bandwidth at 275.64 GB/sec. Redis SET operations perform in the top 10% at 170.81 million operations per second.

While multi-core and parallel execution metrics are highly competitive, single-core performance is moderate, with Geekbench single-core and single-threaded gzip compression falling into the middle 50% category. Additionally, without GPU acceleration, large language model text generation for a 70B model is limited to 2.32 tokens per second. The server offers high resource density for parallel compute tasks, though the 400 GB local NVMe storage is modest relative to the massive 160-core compute allocation.

This hardware profile is suited for highly parallel workloads such as software compilation, multi-threaded data processing, in-memory database operations, and static web serving. It is also capable of handling prompt processing for small to medium language models, though it is not designed for heavy LLM text generation or storage-heavy database deployments.

However, single-core performance and single-threaded compression tasks remain average. Lacking GPU acceleration, it struggles with large LLM text generation, but excels at highly parallelized workloads. The server is suited for software compilation, in-memory databases, and parallel data processing.
